sources.title: About Ad Rank
sources.excerpt: Ad Rank is a set of values that are used to determine whether your ads are eligible to show and if eligible, where on the page your ads are shown (if at all) relative to other advertisers' ads.

evidence.quote: In each auction, your Ad Rank is calculated first to determine whether your ad is eligible to show, and a second time to determine where your ad is ranked relative to other eligible advertisers' ads.
These Ad Rank values are calculated based on several factors, including your competition, the context of the person's search, and your ad quality at that moment.

Your bid - When you set your bid, you're telling Google Ads the maximum amount you're willing to pay for a click on your ad. How much you actually end up paying is often less, and you can change your bid at any time.
Higher quality ads can often lead to lower CPCs. That means you pay less per click when your ads are higher quality.
Ad Rank is calculated every time a user does a search and is recalculated for different positions on the search results page.

Overall, higher quality ads typically lead to lower costs and more advertising success. The Google Ads system works best for everybody when the ads we show are relevant and closely match what customers are searching for.

sources.why_selected: Primary official source for the ad auction and Ad Rank mechanics — the core mechanism explaining why ads cost what they cost, why higher quality can lower CPC, and why ads stop showing when spend or quality falls below threshold.

sources.title: In-Depth Guide to How Google Search Works
sources.excerpt: Google Search is a fully-automated search engine that uses software known as web crawlers that explore the web regularly to find pages to add to our index. In fact, the vast majority of pages listed in our results aren't manually submitted for inclusion, but are found and added automatically when our web crawlers explore the web.

evidence.quote: Google doesn't accept payment to crawl a site more frequently, or rank it higher. If anyone tells you otherwise, they're wrong.

Crawling: Google downloads text, images, and videos from pages it found on the internet with automated programs called crawlers. Indexing: Google analyzes the text, images, and video files on the page, and stores the information in the Google index, which is a large database. Serving search results: When a user searches on Google, Google returns information that's relevant to the user's query.
Google doesn't guarantee that it will crawl, index, or serve your page, even if your page follows the Google Search Essentials.

sources.why_selected: Authoritative Google Search Central doc establishing that organic ranking is fully independent of paid ad spend — directly relevant to the article's claim that stopping ads does not hurt organic rankings, and that organic listing is free.

sources.title: Different Ways to Track Conversions
sources.excerpt: When you run ads with Google Ads, you may want to know whether clicks on your ad led customers to take certain actions such as making a purchase on your website, calling your business, or downloading your app.

evidence.quote:
Website purchases, newsletter signups, button clicks, or other website actions. | Set up your web conversions
Customer installs your app or purchases from your app | Set up your app conversions
Phone calls | Set up your phone call conversions
Offline conversions, such as store visits or phone calls after your ad ran | Set up your offline conversions

Track multiple types of conversions from the list above by creating a separate conversion action for each type. For example, set up one conversion action to track purchases on your website and another to track calls from your ads.

You can also set up multiple conversion actions for each conversion source. For example, if you want to track both purchases and newsletter sign-ups on your website, create one conversion action for purchases and another for sign-ups.

sources.why_selected: Official Google Ads Help doc enumerating current, non-deprecated conversion tracking types. Directly supports the article's 'tracking, not vanity' stance and CTA to set up conversion tracking before spending more.

sources.title: Choose the Right Campaign Type
sources.excerpt: You'll choose a campaign type based on your marketing goals, brand strategy, and how much time you can invest. This article helps you select the right campaign type for your advertising needs.

evidence.quote: Search campaigns are text ads on search results that let you reach people while they're searching on Google for the products and services you offer. It's great for driving sales, leads, or traffic to your website, as you can show your ads to people actively searching for your products and services.

Performance Max is a goal-based campaign type that allows performance advertisers to access all Google Ads inventory from a single campaign. Performance Max helps you drive performance based on your specified conversion goals, delivering more conversions and value by optimizing performance in real time and across channels using Smart Bidding.
Performance Max campaigns are designed to be easy to launch, and when your campaign is live, it'll be optimized by Google AI to drive the best performance possible.

Display campaigns let you reach a relevant audience with visually engaging ads as they browse millions of websites, apps, and Google-owned properties, such as YouTube, to achieve your marketing objectives.

sources.why_selected: Current official campaign-type taxonomy page. Confirms which campaign types are live (Search, Display, Video, App, Shopping, Performance Max) and ties campaign goals to conversion tracking — supporting the article's framing of cost relative to campaign objective.
